citations.claim: After one step vy is -4 m/s, ~6x larger than g*dt=0.667 m/s allows.
Vy keeps growing ~4 m/s per step, reaching -20 m/s by step 5.
First violation: total energy exceeds allowed bound at step 6.

counterfactual.change: Changed only dt from 0.0333333 to 0.0001 (same 6 steps); fast-body substepping no longer inflates gravity, so energy stays ~2020 J and no violation occurs.

explanation: Fast horizontal motion (60 m/s) triggers many substeps per step (68-72). Gravity appears to be integrated with the wrong time scale when substepping is active: vy gains ~4 m/s per 1/30 s step instead of g*dt=0.667 m/s (6x too large), so kinetic + potential energy grows each step with no controller work, eventually exceeding the 10%+5J bound. Small dt removes the excess substepping and the failure disappears.
vision_note: The blue ball travels fast horizontally across the top in frames 3 to 5 then plunges much lower in frame 6. The vertical drop is far larger than the gradual fall in prior frames, indicating a sudden gain in downward velocity.
